title: Forecast Revote and Contract Trigger Procedures
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This page defines the operational process for (1) triggering a forecasting "revote" when material changes or risks to revenue/expense projections occur, and (2) the threshold-based contract review and procurement actions that must happen as a result. The aim is to ensure alignment between FP&A, Sales/Revenue Ops, Legal, Procurement, and Revenue Recognition (RevRec) teams so decisions are timely, auditable, and minimize revenue leakage or compliance risk.

Scope

- Applies to all ARR/commit/one-time contract changes and material forecast updates for Redwood product lines (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private).
- Includes forecasting events impacting expected revenue >= defined thresholds, material cost changes affecting gross margin, and contract amendments that change billing cadence, payment terms, or data-residency requirements.
- Excludes routine sales discounts under delegated approval authority (< $25k ARR impact and within discount matrix).

Definitions

- Revote: A formal re-forecasting process where owners re-submit expected revenue or expense numbers for a given period and obtain explicit FP&A sign-off.
- Contract Trigger: A procurement/legal/finance review required when a contract or amendment crosses a pre-defined financial or policy threshold.
- Materiality thresholds: numeric thresholds (see Decision Matrix) that drive approvals and handoffs.

Decision Matrix (summary)

| Trigger Type | Metric | Action Required | Primary Owner | Escalation/Approver |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Forecast variance | Quarter-to-date revenue variance >= 10% | Revote opened; weekly re-forecast cadence | FP&A (Forecast Manager) | Finance Director (+ Product lead if product variance) |
| New contract / amendment | Annual contract value (ACV) >= $250,000 | Legal + Procurement review; commercial terms worksheet | Sales Ops | Legal Counsel + VP Finance |
| Billing cadence change | Any change from annual to monthly or vice versa | RevRec assessment; billing system change request | Billing Ops | RevRec Manager + Finance Director |
| Data residency / KMS clause | Any customer-requested region or KMS requirement | Security/Compliance review; contract appendix | Legal + Security | Head of Security + Legal Director |
| Capital/one-time hardware spend | Purchase >= $100,000 | Procurement RFQ + budget commit | Purchasing | CFO approval |

When to open a Revote

Open a revote when any of the following occur:

1. Quarter-to-date revenue deviates from last published forecast by >= 10%.
2. Customer churn with ARR impact >= $100k for the quarter.
3. Multiple large bookings (> $250k ACV) are delayed beyond the quarter cutoff.
4. Contract amendments change pricing, billing frequency, or introduce non-standard payment terms.

Procedure: Revote Workflow (step-by-step)

1. Detection and Triage
   - Trigger sources: Sales Ops daily pipeline report, billing exceptions, account executive notification, automated variance alert from forecasting tool.
   - FP&A Forecast Manager logs the revote in the Forecast Tracker (Google Sheet + Jira: FIN-REVOTE-YYYYMMDD).

2. Initial Assessment (24 business hours)
   - FP&A runs a variance breakdown: by account, product, geography, and sales stage.
   - Responsible: Forecast Analyst prepares a one-page memo summarizing causes and initial recommended outlook.

3. Convene Revote Working Group (within 48 hours)
   - Attendees: Forecast Manager (chair), Sales Ops rep, Account Owner(s), Product/Engineering if product-issue driven, Billing Ops, RevRec.
   - Output: Revised P50 and P90 forecasts for the impacted time window and a list of mitigation actions.

4. Documentation and Approval (72 hours)
   - Forecast Manager publishes revised forecast and submits for approval to Finance Director.
   - Finance Director must approve or reject; if rejected, escalate to VP Finance.

5. Communication and Systems Update
   - On approval, Forecast Manager updates the canonical forecast, notifies Execs via the weekly FP&A digest, and files the revote package in the Forecast Archive (shared drive).
   - Billing Ops and RevRec evaluate downstream impacts (billing dates, recognition schedule) and issue change requests to the billing system and GL mapping.

Contract Trigger Procedures

When a contract or amendment meets a trigger in the Decision Matrix, follow the steps below. The objective is to ensure consistent commercial terms, appropriate legal review, and correct RevRec treatment.

1. Intake and Triage
   - Sales Ops submits a Contract Intake form (template in Templates/contract-intake.csv) and attaches proposed SOW/Amendment.
   - Procurement coordinates vendor or third-party evaluation when a hardware or services procurement is part of the deal.

2. Commercial Terms Worksheet
   - Sales Ops populates the Commercial Terms Worksheet (required for ACV >= $50k). Fields: customer name, ACV, billing frequency, payment terms, RPO, termination, pass-through costs, data residency, KMS, warranty SLA.

3. Legal Review and Redlines
   - Legal uses the worksheet to determine clause needs. Standard turnarounds: 3 business days for standard deals, 7 business days for complex deals (KMS, data residency, escrow).

4. RevRec & Billing Assessment
   - RevRec Manager reviews for revenue timing and contract boundaries. If billing cadence changes or variable consideration is introduced, RevRec must sign off before countersignature.

5. Procurement & Payment Terms
   - Procurement validates any vendor-related spend or pass-through costs. For purchase commitments >= $100k, Procurement obtains competitive bids where applicable.

6. Approvals and Countersignature
   - Final approvals per Decision Matrix; Legal files executed contract and notifies Finance and Billing. Countersignature may be delayed only under documented risk mitigation.

Templates and Artifacts (locations)

- Contract Intake Template: /templates/contract-intake.csv
- Commercial Terms Worksheet: /templates/commercial-terms-worksheet.xlsx
- Forecast Tracker (canonical): Drive > Finance > Forecasts > Forecast-Canonical-YYYY.xlsx
- Revote Jira epic prefix: FIN-REVOTE-

Roles & Responsibilities

- Forecast Manager (FP&A): Owner of revote cadence, publishes canonical forecast, coordinates working group.
- Sales Ops: Submits intake forms, provides account-level detail and pipeline status.
- Legal: Reviews contract language, produces redlines, maintains contract repository.
- Procurement: Handles vendor evaluation and purchase order issuance.
- RevRec (Accounting): Certifies recognition treatment, updates revenue schedules.
- Billing Ops: Executes billing system changes and invoice timing updates.

Audit Trail and Controls

- Every revote must have an artifact bundle: notification email thread, one-page memo, revised forecast file, Jira ticket, and list of approvals. Store bundle in Forecast Archive for 7 years.
- Contract redlines and executed copies must be stored in the Contract Repository (DocStore ID required).
- Automated alerts: Forecasting tool sends an immutable snapshot (CSV) to Archive on any revote event.

Sample thresholds (operational reference)

- Forecast revote: revenue delta >= 10% QTD OR absolute ARR change >= $100k.
- Legal review: ACV >= $250k OR any non-standard clause (data residency/KMS/escrow).
- Procurement RFQ: purchase or pass-through cost >= $100k.
- RevRec pre-approval: any change to billing cadence or variable consideration.

Checklist (pre-approval)

- [ ] Contract Intake form complete and attached
- [ ] Commercial Terms Worksheet populated
- [ ] Forecast impact assessed and documented
- [ ] Legal redlines attached or waived in writing
- [ ] RevRec sign-off obtained for recognition timing
- [ ] Procurement bids attached (if applicable)
- [ ] Finance/Director-level approval recorded

Example: Contract language snippet (recommended clause for monthly-to-annual changes)

"If Customer elects to change billing cadence from annual to monthly, any prorations, refunds, or payment deferrals must be documented in an amendment. Changes to billing cadence will be reviewed by Finance and RevRec to confirm revenue recognition treatment; no change will be implemented without written approval from the RevRec Manager."

Edge cases and escalation guidance

- Multiple simultaneous triggers: if a revote coincides with a contract > $250k that also changes data-residency, create a joint working group including Legal, Security, FP&A, and Sales.
- Emergency cutover: for urgent remediation (security, SLA breaches) that require immediate contract amendment, Legal may provisionally approve emergency language with post-hoc FP&A and RevRec review within 5 business days. Document rationale in the Contract Repository.

Operational calendar and SLAs

- Revote detection to Working Group convened: SLA = 48 business hours.
- Forecast Manager to publish revised forecast: SLA = 72 business hours.
- Legal turnaround (standard): 3 business days; complex: 7 business days.
- Procurement RFQ cycle: typical 10 business days for standard procurements.

Reporting and KPIs

- Revote frequency by quarter (% of weeks with revote activity).
- Time-to-approve (median) for revisions and contract triggers.
- Forecast accuracy delta before/after revote.
- Percentage of deals requiring RevRec rework post-signature.

Frequently asked questions

Q: Who owns the canonical forecast during a revote?
A: FP&A (Forecast Manager) retains ownership; inputs come from Sales Ops and account owners.

Q: Can Legal sign a contract if RevRec hasn’t approved the recognition treatment?
A: No—RevRec approval is required whenever billing cadence or variable consideration is altered.
